title: Voices and Sinister Jewel Sockets: 2/3/4 Socket Versions and Which Jewels Fit
summary: Voices is a Unique Sapphire in Path of Exile 2 0.5.4 that allocates 2, 3, or 4 Sinister Jewel Sockets next to your portrait. This guide covers what the number means, where the sockets appear, the no-extra-passive-point cost, why Unique Jewels cannot be slotted, why radius does not apply, how 2/3/4 socket versions compare in value, and how to farm it from the Simulacrum.
description: How Voices works in PoE2 0.5.4: the Unique Sapphire that allocates 2-4 Sinister Jewel Sockets, which jewels fit, why Unique Jewels are excluded, the 2/3/4 socket value curve, and the Simulacrum drop.
author: Exile2 Guides Editorial Team
imageAlt: Path of Exile 2 Voices Unique Sapphire showing the Allocates Sinister Jewel Sockets line and the extra sockets beside the portrait

sections.title: Quick answer
sections.callout: Voices is a Corrupted Unique Sapphire, Limited to 1, that allocates 2, 3, or 4 Sinister Jewel Sockets. These sockets appear directly to the left of your portrait at the centre of the passive skill tree and each holds one regular jewel. It drops only from the Simulacrum (the Grand Mirror at the end of a Simulacrum of Delusion run at 100%+ Deliriousness) and cannot be Chanced or re-rolled.
calloutDetail: The rolled number (2, 3, or 4) is permanent because Voices is already Corrupted - you cannot Vaal, Divine, or re-roll it.
Inserting Voices costs exactly one normal Jewel Socket; the Sinister Sockets it grants do NOT cost extra passive points.
Only regular jewels (Magic/Rare, including Corrupted Magic) fit; Unique Jewels are explicitly excluded from Sinister Sockets.

answers.label: Use for
text: Endgame builds that want more jewel real estate: up to four extra jewel slots from a single passive-tree socket, perfect for stacking life, resistances, attributes, crit, or damage rolls.

answers.label: Check first
text: Confirm the socket count before paying mirror-tier prices, and confirm the jewels you plan to slot are regular (non-Unique) jewels.

answers.label: Avoid
text: Assuming radius, The Adorned, or jewel-socket modifiers apply in Sinister Sockets - they do not. Also never try to slot a Unique jewel or a Megalomaniac there.

facts.label: Base Type
note: Voices is a Unique variant of the Sapphire jewel base that sits in a normal Jewel Socket.

facts.label: Rarity
note: Voices always drops Corrupted, so its socket count is locked at drop and cannot be altered.

facts.label: Limited to
note: You can equip only one Voices, so 4 is the maximum extra Sinister Sockets any character can have.

facts.label: Effect
note: The roll decides the count; it is fixed at drop.

facts.label: Socket location
note: Sinister Jewel Sockets appear next to your Ascendancy portrait at the centre of the passive tree, not on the tree itself.

facts.label: Drop source
note: Drops from the Grand Mirror at the end of a Simulacrum of Delusion run at 100%+ Deliriousness; not Chance Orb compatible.

sections.title: Family overview: the Voices roll
intro: Voices is a single Unique item, but it has three functional variants defined entirely by the rolled socket count. Understanding the number is the whole valuation story.
Each variant is the same jewel with a different 'Allocates N Sinister Jewel Sockets' line. The roll is decided when the jewel drops and is permanent because the item is Corrupted.

members.title: 2-Socket Voices
body: The most common roll. Adds two extra jewel slots. A real but modest ceiling increase; often the entry point because it is far cheaper than higher rolls.

members.title: 3-Socket Voices
body: A strong mid-roll that adds three jewel slots. Trades at a large premium over the 2-socket because each extra slot compounds with well-rolled rares.

members.title: 4-Socket Voices
body: The chase roll. Four extra jewel slots from a single tree socket is one of the highest passive-point yields in the game and commands mirror-tier prices.

properties.label: Base Type

properties.label: Rarity

properties.label: Limited to

sections.title: Valid Jewel Matrix (Sinister vs normal socket)
sections.caption: Which jewel types fit a Sinister Jewel Socket versus a normal Jewel Socket. Cells that depend on client confirmation are marked 'current rule; confirm in client'.
sections.note: The hard, confirmed rule: Unique Jewels cannot be placed in Sinister Jewel Sockets. Regular Magic/Rare jewels fit. Radius effects and jewel-socket modifiers do not apply inside Sinister Sockets, and Sinister Sockets are not within each other's radius.

sections.title: Overview: how Sinister Jewel Sockets work
paragraphs: Voices converts one normal passive-tree Jewel Socket into a source of extra jewel slots. When socketed, it temporarily unlocks 2, 3, or 4 Sinister Jewel Sockets that appear directly to the left of your character's portrait at the centre of the passive skill tree. These sockets are a separate system from the normal sockets scattered around the tree.

Because the number is rolled at drop and Voices is Corrupted, you cannot improve a low roll. The entire price spread between a 2-socket and a 4-socket copy is this single number, which is why identifying (or buying identified) matters so much.

Sinister Sockets are powerful but deliberately constrained. They accept regular jewels only - Unique jewels (including Megalomaniac, The Adorned, Against the Darkness, From Nothing, Controlled Metamorphosis, and Heart of the Well) are excluded. Jewels placed inside them are disconnected from the tree, so they do not benefit from radius effects, jewel-socket passive bonuses, or modifiers that affect Jewel Sockets. Sinister Sockets are also treated as not being within the radius of each other.

Current versus legacy: Voices was introduced in PoE2 0.5.0 as a Delirium-exclusive chase jewel. There is no older 0.1/0.2 version of Voices to compare, but community conclusions about Sinister Socket compatibility that predate 0.5 should not be treated as current. Always verify the socket count and the jewel type against the live 0.5.4 client.
bullets: Voices = 1 normal socket cost, 2/3/4 Sinister Sockets granted.
Sinister Sockets sit by the portrait, not on the tree.
No extra passive points are spent to unlock the Sinister Sockets.
Unique Jewels cannot go in Sinister Sockets; radius does not apply there.
Limited to 1 Voices, so the Sinister Socket ceiling is 4.

sections.title: Socket Count Comparison (2 vs 3 vs 4)
sections.caption: Per-variant cost and value. Voices itself always costs one normal Jewel Socket; the Sinister Sockets it grants are free of passive-point cost.

cells.perjewel: Two clean rares must each beat ~half a high-value tree cluster
cells.single: If your build only benefits from one specific jewel mod, a single high-value normal jewel plus the freed tree path can out-value a 2-socket Voices

cells.perjewel: Three rares must collectively exceed the tree nodes you skip
cells.single: When you only need one or two target mods, the opportunity cost of the tree path can still beat a 3-socket roll
Almost always wins once you have four strong rares; only loses if your build cannot use four independent jewel mods

sections.note: More sockets is not automatically better than one perfectly placed high-value jewel. The decision is about how many independent jewel mods your build can actually use. A 4-socket Voices feeding The Adorned (which amplifies Corrupted Magic jewels) is one of the highest passive-point yields available, but requires the right jewel types.

sections.title: Eligibility: what fits a Sinister Socket
note: Sinister Jewel Sockets are a restricted socket type. The matrix below summarises what is allowed; the single confirmed hard rule is that Unique Jewels cannot be slotted.

steps.label: Unlock a normal Jewel Socket
body: Allocate a normal Jewel Socket on your passive skill tree. Voices occupies this socket like any other jewel.

steps.label: Socket Voices
body: Right-click Voices into the allocated socket. The Sinister Jewel Sockets immediately appear to the left of your portrait.

steps.label: Fill the Sinister Sockets
body: Drag regular Magic/Rare jewels (and, per current client rules, Corrupted Magic jewels) into the Sinister Sockets. Each holds one jewel and grants only its own explicit modifiers.

steps.label: Plan the tree path
body: Because Sinister Sockets cost no extra passive points, the only tree cost is the path to the one socket you gave Voices. Compare that path cost against the stats from your slotted jewels.

before: One normal Jewel Socket holds a single jewel with its own modifiers and any radius effects.
after: That same socket now also grants 2-4 Sinister Sockets by the portrait, each holding an independent regular jewel with no radius dependency.
compare.note: The trade-off is purely the passive points spent reaching Voices' socket versus the cumulative value of 2-4 extra jewels.

rows.scenario: Endgame build with several strong rares
rows.benefit: Turns one tree socket into up to four independent jewel mods
rows.recommendation: A 3-4 socket Voices is a top-tier upgrade for jewel-heavy builds.

rows.scenario: Build needs only one specific jewel mod
rows.recommendation: A single high-value normal jewel plus the freed tree path can out-value a low Voices roll.

rows.benefit: Clear value curve by socket count
rows.recommendation: Buy identified to lock the count, or accept the unID gamble at a discount.

rows.benefit: Four Sinister Sockets can each hold a Corrupted Magic jewel amplified by The Adorned
rows.recommendation: Strong synergy, but confirm Corrupted Magic is allowed in Sinister Sockets in the current client.

sections.title: Build usage
intro: Voices is build-agnostic infrastructure: any character that can use extra jewel mods benefits. The personas below show the main ways to use it.
The decision is not 'more sockets = better' but 'how many independent jewel mods can my build actually use'. A 4-socket Voices is only worth it if you have four worthwhile jewels to fill it.

builds.title: Jewel-stacking endgame
builds.description: Pushes 2-4 clean rares (life, resistances, attributes, crit, damage) through the Sinister Sockets for a large net stat gain.

builds.title: The Adorned corrupted-magic plan
builds.description: Pairs a 4-socket Voices with The Adorned so each Sinister Socket can hold a Corrupted Magic jewel that The Adorned amplifies.

builds.title: Attribute-stacking (Astramentis / HOWA)
builds.description: Uses the extra slots for attribute-heavy rares that complement an attribute-stacking core.

builds.title: Controlled Metamorphosis disconnects
builds.description: Uses the extra slots to place jewels that support ring-allocation setups without spending more tree path.

sections.title: Alternatives
paragraphs: A normal high-value jewel in a regular socket is the direct alternative. If your build only wants one or two specific jewel mods, a single well-placed rare plus the passive points you did NOT spend reaching a Voices socket can out-value a low Voices roll.

Other Unique jewels (The Adorned, Against the Darkness, From Nothing, Controlled Metamorphosis, Megalomaniac) provide their own tree mechanics but cannot be placed in Sinister Sockets, so they are complements rather than replacements for the slots Voices grants.
Time-Lost and Timeless Jewels affect nodes in radius on the tree; they are a different power axis and are also excluded from Sinister Sockets.
bullets: Single high-value normal jewel: flexible, no Voices cost.
Other Unique jewels: complementary tree mechanics, not Sinister-socket fillers.
Time-Lost / Timeless: radius-based tree transformation, different axis.

sections.title: Valuation: use, sell, or hold
marketNote: Prices reflect the Early Access 0.5.4 league on the PC trade site as of early August 2026 and move constantly; confirm the live number on poe.ninja before any large trade.

Value scales steeply with the socket count: a 2-socket copy trades for a few hundred Divine Orbs, a 3-socket for roughly a Mirror, and a 4-socket for several Mirrors. Voices drops unidentified, so the count is hidden until identified.

use.condition: Your build can use 2-4 independent jewel mods and you want more jewel real estate
use.first: Buy an identified copy at the socket count you need, or gamble on an unID at a discount
use.risk: Occupies one tree socket; low rolls are a weak upgrade
text: For jewel-heavy endgame builds a 3-4 socket Voices is one of the biggest single upgrades available.

sell.condition: You found a Voices you cannot use, or want to cash out the unID gamble
sell.first: List identified copies by socket count; sell unID at a discount to transfer the gamble
sell.risk: Liquid but volatile; supply is thin and prices swing with demand
text: It is a chased Simulacrum Unique with steady high-end demand on trade.

hold.condition: You found a high socket-count copy and may build around jewels later
hold.first: Keep it; mirror-tier items retain value across leagues
text: A 4-socket Voices is a long-term asset for jewel-stacking builds.

rows.loss: Paid the unID premium for the weakest variant
rows.recommendation: Compare against identified market prices before identifying; sell unID if you only want 3-4.

rows.scenario: Slotting a Unique jewel by mistake
rows.loss: Wasted time; the game refuses Unique jewels in Sinister Sockets
rows.recommendation: Only prepare regular (Magic/Rare) jewels for Sinister Sockets.

rows.scenario: Assuming radius applies in Sinister Sockets
rows.loss: Mis-valued build; radius jewels do nothing extra there
rows.recommendation: Treat Sinister Sockets as disconnected; value only each jewel's own modifiers.

rows.scenario: Over-investing in a single low roll
rows.loss: Opportunity cost of the tree path vs a single strong jewel
rows.recommendation: Only commit if you can fill most of the granted slots with strong jewels.

entries.question: How many Sinister Sockets does Voices allocate and where do they appear?
summary: Players ask whether the socket count is fixed and where the extra sockets show up on the tree.
editorialAnalysis: Voices allocates 2, 3, or 4 Sinister Jewel Sockets depending on its roll. The sockets appear directly to the left of the character's portrait at the centre of the passive skill tree, not on the tree itself.
officialAnswer: Sinister Jewel Sockets are temporarily unlocked by socketing Voices and sit beside the portrait; the count is rolled at drop.

entries.question: Why can't I put a Unique jewel into a Sinister Socket?
summary: A player tried to slot a Megalomaniac or another Unique into a Sinister Socket and it was rejected.
editorialAnalysis: Unique Jewels cannot be placed in Sinister Jewel Sockets. They are for regular jewels only; jewels inside are also disconnected from radius and jewel-socket modifiers.
officialAnswer: Unique jewels are excluded from Sinister Jewel Sockets by design.

entries.question: Do Sinister Sockets benefit from radius or The Adorned?
summary: Players debated whether a radius jewel in a Sinister Socket still grants radius bonuses.
editorialAnalysis: Jewels in Sinister Sockets are completely disconnected from the skill tree, so they do not benefit from radius effects. The Adorned amplifies Corrupted Magic jewels; whether those may sit in Sinister Sockets should be confirmed in the current client.
officialAnswer: Sinister Sockets are not within radius of anything, including each other; only the jewel's own modifiers apply.

entries.question: Is a 4-socket Voices worth mirror-tier prices?
summary: A video compared the value of 2, 3, and 4 socket copies against single high-value jewels.
editorialAnalysis: More sockets beat one jewel only when the build can use that many independent jewel mods. A 4-socket Voices feeding The Adorned compounding is among the highest passive-point yields, but requires the right jewel types.
officialAnswer: Value scales with socket count and with how many strong jewels you can actually slot.

problems.symptom: My Unique jewel will not go into the Sinister Socket
directAnswer: Unique Jewels cannot be placed in Sinister Jewel Sockets. Use a regular Magic or Rare jewel instead.
checks: Confirm the jewel is not Unique (no Megalomaniac, The Adorned, etc.), then drag a regular jewel in.

problems.symptom: My radius jewel in a Sinister Socket seems to do nothing extra
directAnswer: Sinister Sockets are disconnected from the tree, so radius effects do not apply there. Only the jewel's own explicit modifiers count.
checks: Check that you are valuing only the jewel's own mods, not any radius bonus.

problems.symptom: Voices dropped unidentified and I don't know the count
directAnswer: Voices always drops unidentified and Corrupted. Identify it to reveal 2, 3, or 4; the count is permanent.
checks: Decide whether to identify (lock the count) or sell unID at a discount.

problems.symptom: I equipped Voices but my build feels unchanged
directAnswer: Voices only helps if you fill its Sinister Sockets with strong regular jewels and actually use those mods. Empty or weak sockets give little.
checks: Audit the jewels you slotted; a single high-value normal jewel may beat a low Voices roll.
